Apple has updated the privacy policy of the Apple Store app, adding terms for a yet-to-be-launched virtual shopping assistant. Here are the details.

Apple expands its use of artificial intelligence in retail operations

As discovered by MacRumors, the Apple Store app and its privacy page now include a new section titled "Virtual Shopping Assistant," which states:

In other words, the Apple Store app may eventually incorporate a chatbot that uses user data to provide personalised responses and help users make purchasing decisions.

Apple says it will strip personally identifiable information before sharing conversations with an unnamed partner that provides responses for the assistant, which likely means at least part of the experience will be powered by third-party models from external companies.

Chat records will be retained within the app for users to review, and will also be kept for Apple's business analytics purposes. Users can opt in or out via a new "Chat Improvements" setting to choose whether their conversations can be used to improve the virtual shopping assistant.

The wording of Apple's privacy policy suggests the virtual assistant will initially launch in only a selection of countries and regions, and may debut in English-speaking markets first before gradually expanding to more languages and regions.

This news comes months after Apple added an AI chatbot to its Sales Coach app, which provides sales and technical resources for Apple's retail partners. Users can access the chatbot via the "Ask" tab, where the bot answers questions based on Apple's official training materials and documentation.

Additionally, Bloomberg previously reported that Apple has been testing a system called "Live Notes" at some retail stores, which uses AI to record, transcribe and summarise Genius Bar service sessions, allowing staff to focus on helping customers without being distracted by note-taking.

For more information about the Apple Store app and its privacy policy, please follow this link.
